title: First 24 Hours After Layoff: Practical Checklist
description: A first-day layoff checklist in India: preserve personal records, confirm key dates and payments, protect account access, and choose one practical next step.
lead: Last verified against the listed official sources on 28 October 2026. The checklist is designed to reduce avoidable loss and preserve room for considered decisions.
editorialFrame: The first day after a layoff is a poor time to solve every financial, legal, and career question at once. Focus on records, dates, access, and a short list of written questions. You do not need to make a permanent career decision before you have the basic facts. This guide is a practical sequence for the next 24 hours, not legal advice or a prediction about how quickly another job will arrive.

sections.heading: Pause before responding to a difficult message
sections.content:
If the news arrives in a meeting, ask for the written notice and time to read it. You can request the stated reason, effective date, last working day, payroll end date, benefits end date, and contact for follow-up. Take notes about what was said, who attended, and any deadline. A calm request for time is usually more useful than trying to negotiate every issue while surprised.

Do not sign a statement you do not understand just to finish the meeting. If asked to acknowledge receipt, read what the acknowledgement says and ask whether it records receipt only or also agreement. If you feel pressured or the document has legal consequences, seek qualified advice. Keep the communication factual and respectful, and do not make a public post that discloses private or confidential information.

sections.heading: Secure personal records without taking company data
sections.content:
Before access changes, identify the personal employment records you may lawfully retain: your signed agreement, payslips, tax forms, benefits statements, personal performance feedback, and exit communication. Follow company policy and the law; do not copy source code, customer data, confidential roadmaps, internal mailboxes, or other employer information. If unsure whether a file is personal or company property, ask for an approved copy rather than exporting it yourself.

Use a personal checklist to note account access, devices, keys, and any return instructions. Ask how to retrieve personal items or documents after access ends. Do not forward an entire work mailbox to yourself. Separate what you need to prove employment or pay from material that belongs to the employer. Protecting your own records should not create a new confidentiality or security problem.

sections.heading: Confirm money and benefits as separate questions
sections.content:
Ask for an itemised final-pay statement and the expected date for salary, approved expenses, leave treatment, any severance, and other amounts. Request the document or clause that explains each line. Confirm when health or other benefits end and whether you must take any action. Do not assume every item is due on the same date, or that one gross amount is the same as cash after tax and deductions.

Record amounts as confirmed, pending, or disputed. Keep a copy of the latest payslip and benefit portal details you are permitted to retain. If a payment depends on a condition, write down that condition and who will confirm it. A question about statutory entitlement, tax treatment, or a disputed deduction should be directed to a qualified adviser or the relevant official source with your actual documents.

sections.heading: Protect the accounts you own
sections.content:
Check personal email, phone number, banking access, password manager, and two-factor recovery methods. Update an account only if it is yours and you are authorised to do so; never use company credentials or try to regain access to systems after permission ends. If a personal account uses a work email for recovery, move the recovery route while you still control it and record the change.

If you used a work device for personal files, ask for the approved return or transfer process. Do not bypass company controls or remove management software. Return equipment with a receipt or written confirmation, and keep personal financial accounts separate from employer portals. These steps protect continuity without copying material that you are not allowed to keep.

sections.heading: Make a short cash plan, not a long forecast
sections.content:
List liquid savings, essential monthly costs, debt payments, dependants, and any confirmed final amounts. Leave unconfirmed severance, future bonus, equity, and possible new income outside the available-cash total. Choose one conservative scenario for the next month, then note which costs could be paused or renegotiated. The purpose is to identify the next useful conversation, not to calculate exactly how long a job search will take.

If you are sharing household expenses, tell the people who need to plan with you using the facts you know and the questions still open. Avoid irreversible choices such as a large withdrawal, loan, or sale made solely to ease the first shock. A qualified financial or tax adviser can help with decisions involving debt, benefits, or tax consequences.

sections.heading: Send one clear follow-up email
sections.content:
After you have had time to read the notice, send a concise message listing unanswered items: effective date, final working day, handover, payroll and benefits dates, final-pay statement, equipment return, and the person responsible for each answer. Ask for a response date if a decision is time-sensitive. Keep a copy of the message and reply. Do not send personal identifiers or sensitive financial details beyond what is necessary.

If the employer gives different answers through separate channels, ask one authorised contact to reconcile them in writing. Note what is confirmed and what remains provisional. Do not confuse an automated portal status with the final interpretation of a contract or a statutory entitlement. If a dispute or short deadline arises, obtain individual advice promptly rather than relying on a generic checklist.

sections.heading: Choose only the next reversible action
sections.content:
For the rest of the first day, choose one or two manageable actions: update the cash list, tell a trusted person, schedule a follow-up call, or write down the work you want to explore next. You are not required to turn a layoff into an immediate personal-brand project. Leave space to sleep, eat, and process the news; practical judgment is harder when every decision is treated as urgent.

The next step can be a short task, not a full career plan. The Layoff Hub offers a runway worksheet and dated source context; it does not tell you whether a company will rehire or how soon a new role will appear. Use your own needs and support network to choose what comes next.

nextSteps: Save the notice and lawful personal employment records, and write down effective, working, payroll, and benefits dates that need confirmation.
Request an itemised final-pay statement and a named contact for questions; label each amount confirmed, pending, or disputed instead of guessing.
Make a one-month essential-cost list and choose one reversible next action; defer major financial or career decisions until the missing facts are clearer.

sourceDisclosure: A practical checklist, not legal, tax, financial, or mental-health advice. Preserve only records you may lawfully keep and seek qualified support for individual questions.

faqs.question: Should I sign the layoff letter immediately?
faqs.answer: Read what the document says. If it is more than receipt or you are unsure of its effect, ask for time and qualified advice.

faqs.question: What work files should I download?
faqs.answer: Do not copy company or customer information. Ask for approved copies of personal employment and pay records you may retain.

faqs.question: Should I start applying the same day?
faqs.answer: You can, but you do not have to. First confirm dates and documents, then choose a manageable next step.

faqs.question: Is severance included in final salary?
faqs.answer: Treat them as separate line items until the employer provides an itemised statement and explains the relevant terms.
